document.title: DCI UBL Update
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: [Top Secret] CIA DCI update on bin Laden (UBL). Cited in 9/11 Commission Report Chapter 4, Endnote 188. An excerpt is the briefing book's cover image.

organizations.name: Central Intelligence Agency
organizations.notes: Author of the briefing; the slides refer to the DCI, the Director of Central Intelligence.

organizations.name: Alec Station
organizations.notes: The resources slide on p.15 names it. It is the CIA unit that tracks UBL.

organizations.name: FBI
organizations.notes: Slide p.12 notes excellent cooperation with FBI headquarters and at the working level. It also says the FBI is adding to a task force (TF).

events.description: The DCI briefing 'UBL Update' on disrupting UBL operations. Its sections cover new developments, IC issues, looking ahead (staffing, Alec Station resources) and rethinking. The text is largely illegible OCR.

The Director of Central Intelligence (DCI) receives a briefing titled 'UBL Update'. It covers disrupting UBL operations, new developments, intelligence community issues, staffing and resources for Alec Station, and a rethinking of capture options.

relationships.detail: The slides note good cooperation with FBI headquarters and at the working level, apparently with CIA elements. The text is garbled, so the pairing is inferred.
relationships.quote: Excellent ... action with FBI/HQS ... and at the working level

relationships.detail: Alec Station resources are discussed in a CIA DCI briefing on disrupting UBL operations, which implies it is a CIA unit.
The briefing is titled 'Disrupting UBL Operations' and discusses a possible UBL capture operation or ambush, so the CIA is working against bin Laden's network.
relationships.quote: Not Capable of Mounting a UBL Capture Operation or Ambush

key_claims: The slides are about disrupting UBL operations, with sections on new developments, intelligence community issues, and looking ahead.
Staffing and Alec Station resources are named as problems needing attention.
The slides say a fundamental rethinking is needed.
The 'Rethinking' slide appears to say the capability to mount a UBL capture operation or ambush is lacking. It also mentions reporters on the ground, but the OCR is garbled.
The intelligence community process is described as bureaucratic. A bi-weekly meeting is mentioned to improve communications, and cooperation with the FBI is called excellent.
